segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate, as the index maps 'any motor vehicle'.

The movement of the motor vehicle is its motion: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the vehicle moving, above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed', whose braking shows the movement disturbed; it is 'Not a stand-in for: speed', and it is read here as the change the interference forces, not as the speed. The rider interferes from in front of the vehicle's movement: rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', with the rider's bearing in the vehicle's frame pointing ahead. No exclusion applies.

operationalizations.standard: intentionally interfere (intent, a state of mind, and the degree of interference)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: an interference with a vehicle's movement is a conflict in which the vehicle, with the rider ahead of it, brakes evasively — a deceleration beyond comfortable service braking while their closest approach lies within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
obligation: At every observation, for every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), it is not the case that: the subject lies ahead of m (the longitudinal component of the subject's rel.bearing in m's frame is positive), m's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below the negative of p.vehicle_evasive_decel, and prim.closest_approach_within(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.

Intent shows in no single observation: it is read only through the conduct that interferes — the rider ahead of a moving motor vehicle in a conflict that forces it to brake evasively — and a conflict the rider did not seek is not told apart; an interference that forces no evasive braking (a swerve only) is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle cuts in front of a moving car and slows; the car, with the bicycle ahead of it, brakes harder than p.vehicle_evasive_decel while their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides in a bicycle lane; a car passes it without braking and without a conflicting closest approach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a car (not a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregates).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter swerves in front of a moving car with a conflicting closest approach; the car's longitudinal acceleration is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a path with no motor vehicle in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_evasive_decel
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration of a motor vehicle at or beyond which its braking counts as an evasive reaction to another road user rather than ordinary speed control: about 0.4 g, above the comfortable deceleration of about 3.4 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate; traffic-conflict studies of evasive braking

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
